title: Re-queued gen_render rows never start after a restart
body:
## Summary
main.ts resumes the job runner before it registers gen_render, so a gen_render row a restart put back to queued has no mover and the generation worker polls it forever.

## Description
apps/server/src/main.ts:49 calls runner.resume() and apps/server/src/main.ts:57 registers gen_render afterwards. resume() only pumps kinds that have a handler at that moment, and register() (apps/server/src/jobs.ts:56) never pumped, so the row waited for an unrelated render on the shared lane. waitForRender (apps/server/src/generation/render-steps.ts) has no timeout, by design (a server restart mid-render must not fail the job). DESIGN §3 promises tsx-watch restarts resume interrupted jobs. Violates job-coordination/terminal-state-recovery (every non-terminal state names its mover). Fixed: register() after resume() pumps its kind (apps/server/src/jobs.ts:59).

## Flow
- owner saves a server file while a generation job renders -> tsx watch SIGTERM -> gen_render row re-queued (interrupted by shutdown)
- new process: resume() pumps render/llm/... but gen_render has no handler yet -> returns
- register('gen_render') -> nothing starts it -> worker polls renderStatus forever

## Expected impact
Generation jobs that were rendering during a dev restart finish instead of hanging; measured by the new jobs.test case. Could break: a kind registered after resume now starts at registration time (intended; registering before resume is unchanged and pinned).

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - a re-queued row of a late-registered kind runs
Before: row stays 'queued' after resume + late register (test red: Expected succeeded, Received queued)
After: row runs and succeeds; 17/17 jobs tests
Method: gate - new jobs.test case seeded red before the fix
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: jobs.test.ts 'a kind registered after resume() ... still runs its re-queued rows' (red before)

title: POST /keyframes bypasses the render_keyframes tool schema
body:
## Summary
The HTTP twin of the render_keyframes tool passed any frames_s straight to the renderer, while the MCP and replay doors enforce MAX_FRAMES and seconds >= 0.

## Description
apps/server/src/tool-schemas.ts holds one zod shape per tool and tools.test pins 'one schema for replay and live'. apps/server/src/app.ts (keyframes route, now :172) cast the body and called Pipeline.renderKeyframes with whatever frames_s was: 7+ frames, negative seconds, or undefined. mcp-tools/tool-schema-design: a constraint lives in the schema every door runs. Fixed: the route runs parseToolInput('render_keyframes') and answers 400 with the issues.

## Flow
- a local process POSTs {frames_s: [0..50]} with application/json (the guard admits no-Origin JSON)
- route -> Pipeline.renderKeyframes -> one still per frame, no cap

## Expected impact
The renderer can no longer be asked for more stills through HTTP than through MCP. Could break: a caller sending more than 6 frames now gets 400 (zero in-tree callers: grep '/keyframes').

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - one rule enforced at every door
Before: 0 of 4 bad bodies refused (7 frames, [-1], {}, [])
After: 4 of 4 -> 400 naming frames_s, renderer never called; valid body unchanged
Method: gate - app.errors.test 'POST /keyframes refuses what render_keyframes refuses' red then green
Result: better
Gate: policy-tighten
evidence:
apps/server/src/tool-schemas.ts render_keyframes: z.array(z.number().min(0)).min(1).max(MAX_FRAMES)
apps/server/src/app.ts:172-177 (before: body.frames_s passed unchecked)
grep -rn '/keyframes' -> only the route itself
instrument: app.errors.test.ts 'HTTP doors validate like their tool twins'

title: Job lists in GET /api/jobs and /api/projects are sliced in JS
body:
## Summary
Both routes read every job row and sliced in JS although JobRunner.list takes a SQL LIMIT.

## Description
apps/server/src/jobs.ts list(projectId, limit) pushes ORDER BY / LIMIT into SQL (pinned by jobs.test), but apps/server/src/app.ts called list().slice(0, 50) for /api/jobs and list(p.id).slice(0, 5) per project for /api/projects - an abstraction with un-migrated call sites. Fixed: both pass the limit (apps/server/src/app.ts:129, :331).

## Flow
- studio polls /api/jobs and /api/projects
- each call materialised the whole jobs table (params/result JSON) to keep 50 / 5 rows

## Expected impact
Studio job lists cost ~10x less server time on a large jobs table; responses identical. Could break: nothing - same rows, same order.

## Evaluation
Claim: performance - rows materialised per request
Before: probe 5000 rows: /api/jobs 15.59 ms; 50 projects 12.88 ms
After: 1.22 ms; 3.49 ms (same probe, same calls); test pins list(undefined, 50) and list(p, 5)
Method: probe (timed path on a 5000-row :memory: db) + gate (call-shape test red before)
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
apps/server/src/app.ts:129 d.runner.list(p.id, 5) (was list(p.id).slice(0, 5))
apps/server/src/app.ts:331 d.runner.list(undefined, 50) (was list().slice(0, 50))
instrument: app.errors.test.ts 'job lists are cut in SQL, not in JS' + scratchpad timing probe

title: Malformed STATREEL_ALLOWED_ORIGINS fails per request, not at boot
body:
## Summary
A scheme-less allowed-origin entry either throws 'Invalid URL' on every request whose Host reaches it or silently never matches; the studio port was unchecked too.

## Description
apps/server/src/http-guard.ts allowedOrigins() added entries verbatim and checkRequest runs new URL(o) per request (apps/server/src/http-guard.ts:57). The env-validated-at-boot direction covered config.ts keys but not the guard's three (STATREEL_ALLOWED_ORIGINS, STATREEL_STUDIO_PORT, E2E_STUDIO_PORT). settings/typed-accessors: parse once at the boundary. Fixed: allowedOrigins (built once in serve.ts) throws one error naming the key; entries stored as the browser's origin serialization; empty port counts as unset.

## Flow
- owner sets STATREEL_ALLOWED_ORIGINS=127.0.0.1:3000
- a request with Host 127.0.0.1:3000 -> new URL('127.0.0.1:3000') throws -> 500
- STATREEL_ALLOWED_ORIGINS=localhost:3000 -> parses as scheme 'localhost:' -> the origin is silently 403'd

## Expected impact
A typo stops the server with a readable message instead of 500s or silent 403s. Could break: a previously tolerated junk entry now refuses to boot (intended).

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - config errors surface at boot
Before: probe: 2 of 2 malformed spellings misbehave per request (THROW Invalid URL / 403)
After: 2 of 2 stop at boot naming STATREEL_ALLOWED_ORIGINS; http://127.0.0.1:3000 unchanged (200)
Method: gate - http-guard.test new case red then green; probe re-run on the real change
Result: better
Gate: policy-tighten
evidence:
apps/server/src/http-guard.ts:24 allowedOrigins
apps/server/src/http-guard.ts:57 new URL(o).port per request
probe before: "127.0.0.1:3000" GET THROW Invalid URL
instrument: http-guard.test.ts 'a malformed STATREEL_ALLOWED_ORIGINS entry or studio port is a boot error'

title: Boot sweep is silent and crash re-queues carry no reason
body:
## Summary
resume() re-queued rows a dead process left running without recording why, discarded the retention counts, and logged nothing.

## Description
apps/server/src/jobs.ts resume() set status queued with error untouched, while a graceful stop writes 'interrupted by shutdown' (apps/server/src/jobs.ts:147); retain() threw the prune counts away. background-jobs/startup-sweeps 'Attributed, always': a silent sweep is indistinguishable from one that did not run. Fixed: crash re-queues record INTERRUPTED_BY_EXIT (apps/server/src/jobs.ts:29); retain() returns counts; resume() returns {requeued, pruned} and logs one counted line.

## Flow
- server crashes mid-render
- next boot re-queues the row with error null and prints nothing
- the render reruns; nothing says it was interrupted

## Expected impact
The owner can see after any restart how many jobs were re-run and what retention removed. Could break: queued rows now carry an error text - the studio paints job.error only for failed/refused/cancelled (apps/studio/src/studio/shared.tsx, projectState.ts).

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - the boot repair leaves evidence
Before: crash re-queue error null; 0 startup lines; counts discarded (test red)
After: reason recorded; '[jobs] startup: re-queued N ...; pruned J ...' logged; counts returned
Method: gate - jobs.test 'the boot sweep is attributed' red then green
Result: better
Gate: policy-tighten
evidence:
apps/server/src/jobs.ts:171 resume(): { requeued, pruned }
apps/server/src/jobs.ts:29 INTERRUPTED_BY_EXIT

title: POST /api/projects kept its own catch: DB failures reported as 400
body:
## Summary
One route still used a raw inline catch that answers every failure 400 with the raw message, so a database fault on project create blamed the owner's input and was never logged.

## Description
The pass-2 error mapping routed inline catches through bad() (mapError with a 400 fallback; SqliteError -> logged 500). POST /api/projects kept 'catch (e) { return c.json({ error }, 400) }'. error-handling/error-doors. Fixed: it calls bad(), now declared next to onError (apps/server/src/app.ts:100). Commit body figures read '1 raw / 16 via bad' -> '0 / 17'; the re-counted figures are 1 raw / 17 via bad -> 0 / 18.

## Flow
- database locked during New project
- route -> 400 'database is locked', nothing logged
- studio tells the owner the input was wrong

## Expected impact
DB faults on create surface as server errors with a stack in the log. Could break: nothing - plain input errors stay 400.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - one error door
Before: 1 raw inline catch / 17 via bad(); SqliteError -> 400 unlogged (test red)
After: 0 raw / 18 via bad(); SqliteError -> 500 'database error' + logged
Method: gate - app.errors.test 'POST /api/projects reports through the shared error door'
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence: grep -c 'catch (e) { return c.json({ error' app.ts: 1 -> 0; grep -c 'return bad(c, e)': 17 -> 18
instrument: app.errors.test.ts 'a database failure is a logged 500, bad input stays 400'

title: Malformed body on /llm or /produce starts a default run
body:
## Summary
A truncated or malformed JSON body to the co-pilot or produce route was read as 'no body' and started a run with defaults.

## Description
apps/server/src/app.ts read both optional bodies with c.req.json().catch(() => ({})): /llm then started a co-pilot session with the draft prompt (live and paid under LLM_MODE=live; a follow-up silently became a new session), /produce rendered on the default youtube/monetized target; prompt/session types were unchecked. Fixed: optionalJson() (apps/server/src/app.ts:78) - empty body = defaults, a present body must parse (SyntaxError -> 400) and be an object; /llm refuses non-string prompt/session.

## Flow
- client sends '{"prompt": "make the bars blue", "session": "s1"' (truncated)
- catch -> {} -> llm.start(id, undefined, undefined) -> new paid session with the draft prompt

## Expected impact
A broken request can no longer spend a co-pilot run or start a render the owner did not ask for. Could break: a caller sending invalid JSON now gets 400 (studio always sends a JSON object).

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - malformed input never starts work
Before: 2 of 2 routes started work on a malformed body; prompt: 42 accepted (test red)
After: 3 of 3 bad bodies -> 400, nothing started; empty body still uses defaults
Method: gate - app.errors.test 'an optional JSON body is optional, not ignorable'
Result: better
Gate: policy-tighten
evidence:
apps/server/src/app.ts (before) const body = (await c.req.json().catch(() => ({}))) on /llm and /produce
apps/server/src/app.ts:78 optionalJson
instrument: app.errors.test.ts 'an optional JSON body is optional, not ignorable'

title: No index serves the all-projects job list ordering
body:
## Summary
ORDER BY created_at with no project filter scanned the jobs table and sorted it in a temp B-tree.

## Description
apps/server/src/db.ts had jobs_project_created (project_id, created_at) and jobs_status_kind_created; neither serves GET /api/jobs. Fixed: jobs_created on jobs(created_at) (apps/server/src/db.ts:302), additive and idempotent.

## Flow
- studio polls /api/jobs
- SQLite: SCAN jobs | USE TEMP B-TREE FOR ORDER BY

## Expected impact
The list query uses an index; ~1 ms saved per poll at 5000 rows. Could break: one more index to maintain on job insert (rare writes).

## Evaluation
Claim: performance - query plan of the job list
Before: plan SCAN + TEMP B-TREE; 1.30 ms at 5000 rows
After: SCAN USING INDEX jobs_created; 0.15 ms
Method: probe (explain + timing) + gate (jobs.test index case forbids the temp B-tree, red before)
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence: apps/server/src/db.ts:302 create index if not exists jobs_created on jobs(created_at);
instrument: jobs.test.ts 'the list / pump / project queries use the jobs indexes'

title: POST /policy-probe trusts with_source unchecked
body:
## Summary
A missing with_source was a TypeError 500 and a partial one reached the OPA input with undefined licence fields.

## Description
apps/server/src/app.ts cast the body and passed body.with_source to Pipeline.policyProbe, which pushes it into the manifest's sources. Fixed: ProbeSourceSchema (apps/server/src/app.ts:46) requires id, license_class, verdict as non-empty strings -> 400 naming with_source.<field>. error-handling/user-facing-mapping.

After: 2 of 2 -> 400, pipeline not called; full body unchanged

title: A stored-JSON parse failure on a GET reads as '400 malformed JSON'
body:
## Summary
mapError turns every SyntaxError into a 400 blaming the request, so a corrupt stored row on a GET told the studio its (bodyless) request was malformed.

## Description
apps/server/src/app.ts mapError maps SyntaxError -> 400 because the body parser throws one; 11 JSON.parse sites in services read on GET routes (projects, board, library, llm-service, heatmap-service, calendar) can throw it from stored data. error-handling/taxonomy-design: caller fault and server fault are different kinds. Fixed: onError answers GET/HEAD SyntaxErrors as a logged 500 'stored data could not be read: ...' (apps/server/src/app.ts:92).

## Flow
- a props_json row is corrupt
- GET /api/projects/:id -> 400 'malformed JSON: Unexpected token' and no log

## Expected impact
A corrupt row is reported as a server fault with a stack, not as the owner's mistake. Could break: none for POST bodies (still 400).

## Evaluation
Claim: user - the message names the right cause
Before: GET SyntaxError -> 400 'malformed JSON', unlogged (test red)
After: 500 'stored data could not be read: ...' + logged
Method: gate - app.errors.test 'a SyntaxError on a GET is the server's stored JSON'
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
apps/server/src/app.ts:92 bodyless = GET|HEAD
JSON.parse counts: projects 2, board 1, library 1, llm-service 1, heatmap-service 2, calendar 4

title: A second Ctrl-C cannot interrupt a hung graceful shutdown
body:
## Summary
Every SIGINT/SIGTERM re-entered the memoized graceful stop, so a second signal during a ~12 s stop did nothing.

## Description
apps/server/src/shutdown.ts installProcessHandlers ran shutdown().finally(exit(0)) per signal. subprocess-lifecycle/termination-and-reaping: a polite stop must have a point where it becomes a kill. Fixed: the first signal starts the graceful stop, a second exits 1 at once (apps/server/src/shutdown.ts:48); interrupted rows are repaired by resume() with the attributed reason.

## Flow
- a job handler ignores its abort
- owner presses Ctrl-C -> graceful stop waits up to 10 s + 2 s
- second Ctrl-C -> nothing

## Expected impact
The owner's terminal is never held hostage by a stuck handler. Could break: a double SIGTERM from a supervisor now skips the WAL checkpoint (SQLite WAL is crash-safe; resume() repairs rows).

## Evaluation
Claim: user - a stop the owner can force
Before: second SIGINT during a hung stop -> no exit (test red)
After: exit(1) at once; shutdown() called once; existing handler tests unchanged
Method: gate - shutdown.test 'a second SIGINT/SIGTERM ... exits at once'
Result: better
Gate: none

title: runWorker drops a final stdout line that has no newline
body:
## Summary
The worker protocol reader only parsed newline-terminated lines and discarded the remainder at close, so an unterminated done message turned a success into 'exited 0'.

## Description
apps/server/src/render-support.ts split stdout on '\n'; 'close' ignored buf. render-worker.mjs writes '\n' today, so this hardens the contract. Fixed: one onLine() handler, fed the remainder at close (apps/server/src/render-support.ts:120).

## Flow
- worker ends with process.stdout.write(JSON.stringify({type:'done'})) and exits 0
- runWorker rejects 'render worker exited 0'

## Expected impact
A render can no longer fail on a lost final newline. Could break: nothing - complete lines are handled as before.

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - protocol edge at process exit
Before: unterminated done -> rejected (test red)
After: resolves with done; 12/12 render-support tests
Method: gate - render-support.test 'a last line without a trailing newline is still read'
Result: better
Gate: none

title: A second server on the same app.sqlite double-runs a live job
body:
## Summary
createServer() resumes the runner before serve() binds the port, and the resume re-queues every 'running' row with a blind write, so a second server process on the default DB re-runs the live server's job before its own port bind fails.

## Description
apps/server/src/serve.ts:10 awaits createServer() (which calls runner.resume(), apps/server/src/main.ts:49) before apps/server/src/serve.ts:11 binds. resume() re-queues WHERE status='running' with no owner check (apps/server/src/jobs.ts:171) and pump() claims with an unconditional update by id (apps/server/src/jobs.ts:214). background-jobs/startup-sweeps: repairs are compare-and-set, not blind writes; job-coordination/lease-renewal. A second `pnpm dev`/`pnpm start` in another terminal (the default STATREEL_APP_DB) is enough. Fix options: bind the port before resume (serve.ts/main.ts), and/or an instance lease + CAS claim (status='queued') in pump.

## Flow
- pnpm dev runs a render (row running)
- owner starts pnpm start in a second terminal
- second process: resume() re-queues the live row, pumps it, spawns a second render (or a second publish upload)
- then its listen fails EADDRINUSE -> uncaught -> shutdown

## Expected impact
No job (render, publish, LLM run) can be executed twice by two processes on one DB. Could break: boot order changes touch the e2e webServer readiness and the worker callbacks.

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - one job, one execution
Before: experiment: one enqueued job, two runners on one file DB -> handler starts ['live','second']
After: not yet built: the same harness should show ['live'] only
Method: experiment - scratchpad harness with two JobRunners on one SQLite file; gate not reached because the fix is M across serve.ts/main.ts/jobs.ts
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
apps/server/src/serve.ts:10 const s = await createServer();  // resume inside
apps/server/src/serve.ts:11 serve({...})  // bind after
apps/server/src/jobs.ts:214 set({ status: "running" }).where(eq(jobs.id, next.id))  // no status CAS
probe: handler starts for one enqueued job: [ 'live', 'second' ]
instrument: jobs.test case: two JobRunners on one temp-file DB, second.resume() while the first runs -> exactly one handler start; plus a serve-order test that resume() runs only after listen succeeded

title: ingest/transform are runner job kinds that nothing can run
body:
## Summary
JobKind, DESIGN §3 and the studio all treat ingest and transform as runner jobs, but no handler is registered and no code enqueues them, so a queued row of either kind would sit forever with no age policy.

## Description
packages/schemas/src/index.ts:318 JobKind includes ingest and transform; DESIGN.md §3 'Single-slot job runner: jobs (ingest, transform, audio, render, publish, metrics)'; apps/studio/src/events.ts:76 refreshes on their job.succeeded; apps/server registers only llm, audio, render, publish, metrics, gen_render (grep runner.register). JobRunner.idle() ignores unregistered kinds. job-coordination/terminal-state-recovery: queued needs an age policy for queues nobody drains. Deciding whether the server should run ingest/transform (a Python bridge through the ethics-layer clients) or the kinds should leave the enum and the doc is a capability call.

## Flow
- anyone enqueues 'transform' (typed as valid)
- no handler -> pump returns -> row queued forever; idle() does not see it

## Expected impact
Either the studio gets a real ingest/transform button through the runner, or the contract stops promising one. Could break: removing kinds touches the schema package and studio labels.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - declared capability matches the code
Before: 2 of 8 JobKinds have no handler and no producer; DESIGN and studio name them
After: decision needed before a figure exists
Method: simulation - three walked sites (schema enum, DESIGN §3, studio events.ts); a gate needs the direction first
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: direction
evidence:
packages/schemas/src/index.ts:318 JobKind = z.enum(["ingest", "transform", ...])
apps/studio/src/events.ts:76 e.kind === "ingest" || e.kind === "transform"
grep runner.register -> llm, audio, render, publish, metrics, gen_render
instrument: owner direction: wire ingest/transform as runner jobs (ethics-layer Python bridge) or drop them from JobKind + DESIGN §3 + studio
